headline: Anthropic reports task-level patterns in scientists’ use of Claude
summary: Anthropic’s 5 November 2026 report analyzes 207,049 consumer-plan Claude and Claude Code sessions classified as scientific work from 2 August to 30 September. It reports that data analysis and writing are common uses, while data gathering and ideation appear less often than their estimated share of researcher time. An LLM-based task-capability measure is associated with greater use: the top fifth of tasks receive about two to four times the use expected from researcher time. A separate survey of 528 active AI-using scientists broadly mirrors the task mix. These are first-party, classifier-based usage findings; the underlying conversations are not public for independent audit. The report does not measure research quality, causal productivity or realized scientific discoveries, and its future-output scenarios are hypothetical.
